target: पंकज अपने परिवार के साथ लखनऊ घूमने गया।
english: Pankaj went to visit Lucknow with his family.
tip: के साथ (ke saath) = physically 'with': परिवार के साथ (parivaar ke saath = with his family). Don't mix it up with के पास (ke paas), which means 'near' or 'have'.

target: कविता ने अपने आप यह सारा काम पूरा किया।
english: Kavita completed all this work by herself.
tip: अपने आप (apne aap) = by oneself: Kavita finished सारा काम (saara kaam = all the work) with no help. For things, the same phrase means 'on its own'.

target: आख़िर विकास ने अपनी बात मनवा ही ली।
english: In the end, Vikas managed to get his way.
tip: मनवा ही ली (manva hi li) – मानना (maanna = accept) plus -वा means getting OTHERS to accept: Vikas didn't just state अपनी बात (apni baat = his point), he made them agree.

target: निखिल, मत जाओ ना, यहीं तो रुको।
english: Nikhil, don't go, stay right here.
tip: ना (na) tacked onto a command doesn't negate – it softens it into a plea: मत जाओ ना (mat jao na) = 'please don't go'.

target: उन्हें शोर-शराबा बिलकुल पसंद नहीं।
english: They don't like noise at all.
tip: Hindi often drops है (hai) after a negative: पसंद नहीं (pasand nahin) alone means 'doesn't like it' – no 'is' needed at the end.

target: रेलवे फाटक बंद होने पर रुक जाओ।
english: Stop when the railway crossing gate is closed.
tip: जाना (jaana = go) glued onto a verb marks completion: रुक जाओ (ruk jao) = come to a full stop. Plain रुको (ruko) is just 'stop'.

target: यह शहर उतना साफ़ नहीं जितना पहले था।
english: This city is not as clean as it used to be.
tip: 'Not as...as' is a matched pair in Hindi: उतना साफ़ नहीं जितना (utna saaf nahin jitna) = literally 'not that-much clean, as-much-as'. Two words where English repeats 'as'.

target: कमला को कहीं भी शांति नहीं मिलती।
english: Kamala does not find peace anywhere.
tip: Hindi says 'anywhere + not' where English says 'nowhere': कहीं भी शांति नहीं मिलती (kahin bhi shanti nahin milti) = literally 'anywhere peace is not found'.

target: न प्रिया आई, न कोई संदेश भेजा।
english: Neither did Priya come, nor did she send any message.
tip: न...न (na...na) means 'neither...nor' – a third negator besides नहीं (nahin) and मत (mat): न प्रिया आई, न कोई संदेश (na Priya aayi, na koi sandesh).

target: मुझे तो तैरना आता ही नहीं।
english: I just can't swim at all.
tip: Skills 'come' to you in Hindi: तैरना आता ही नहीं (tairna aata hi nahin) = literally 'swimming just doesn't come (to me)' = I can't swim. आना (aana = to come) covers know-how.

target: पार्किंग में जगह नहीं मिली, दूर खड़ी की।
english: I didn't find space in the parking, so I parked far away.
tip: Cars 'stand' in Hindi: खड़ी की (khari ki) = parked, literally 'made it stand'. गाड़ी खड़ी करना (gaadi khari karna) = to park a car.

target: मैंने अभी तक वह फ़िल्म नहीं देखी।
english: I haven't seen that film yet.
tip: 'Not yet' = अभी तक...नहीं (abhi tak...nahin), literally 'until now not': मैंने अभी तक वह फ़िल्म नहीं देखी (maine abhi tak vah film nahin dekhi) = I haven't seen that film yet.

target: यहाँ सिगरेट मत पियो।
english: Don't smoke here.
tip: You 'drink' a cigarette in Hindi: सिगरेट मत पियो (cigarette mat piyo) = don't smoke, literally 'don't drink a cigarette'. पीना (peena) covers smoking too.

target: देर मत करना, मैं बाहर इंतज़ार कर रहा हूँ।
english: Don't be late, I'm waiting outside.
tip: A command built on the infinitive is for later or gentler: देर मत करना (der mat karna) = 'don't be late (when the time comes)'. मत करो (mat karo) orders it right now.

target: बोतल में ठंडा पानी भरा है।
english: The bottle is filled with cold water.
tip: English fills the bottle – Hindi flips it: बोतल में ठंडा पानी भरा है (botal mein thanda paani bhara hai = in the bottle cold water is filled). The container gets में (mein), the water is the subject.

target: बाज़ार यहाँ से कितनी दूर है?
english: How far is the market from here?
tip: Hindi position words come after their word, not before: यहाँ से (yahaan se = here from) = from here. Every from, on, in trails its word – mez par, subah se.

target: सुप्रभात! आज नाश्ते में क्या बनाया?
english: Good morning! What did you make for breakfast?
tip: For breakfast is नाश्ते में (naashte mein = in breakfast), not ke liye. Meals take में (mein): you make things in breakfast, in lunch.

target: यहाँ से हवाई अड्डा कैसे जाएँ?
english: How do I get to the airport from here?
tip: No word for to with going: हवाई अड्डा कैसे जाएँ (hawai adda kaise jaaen = how to go airport). Destinations of jaana usually take nothing – ghar jao, school jao.

target: फ्रिज में दूध रखा है।
english: There is milk in the fridge.
tip: Hindi says where things are placed, not that they exist: फ्रिज में दूध रखा है (fridge mein doodh rakha hai = milk is kept in the fridge) is the everyday way to say there is milk.

target: शोभा शाम तक घर पहुँच जाएगी।
english: Shobha will reach home by evening.
tip: तक (tak) means both until and by: शाम तक (shaam tak) here is by evening – a deadline. Shaam tak kaam kiya would be until evening. Context picks the reading.

target: गाड़ी दो नंबर प्लेटफ़ॉर्म से चलती है।
english: The train leaves from platform two.
tip: Trains walk in Hindi: चलती है (chalti hai = moves) is how the train departs from the platform. चलना (chalna) covers vehicles and machines – a working watch chalti hai too.

target: मेरे फूफाजी सेना में अफ़सर हैं।
english: My uncle is an officer in the army.
tip: English lumps all uncles together – Hindi is precise: फूफाजी (phoophaji) is specifically your father's sister's husband. The जी (ji) on the end adds respect.

target: मुझे दूर-दूर तक घूमना पसंद है।
english: I like to travel far and wide.
tip: Doubling stretches a word: दूर-दूर तक (door-door tak = up to far-far) = far and wide. Hindi repeats words for spread – kabhi-kabhi is sometimes, dheere-dheere is slowly.

target: रूपा से मिलिए, ये मेरी सहेली हैं।
english: Meet Roopa, she is my friend.
tip: Hindi meets from people: रूपा से मिलिए (Roopa se miliye = meet Roopa). मिलना (milna) always takes से (se), never a plain object like English meet.

target: मोहन बस से आगरा तक जाता है।
english: Mohan goes to Agra by bus.
tip: से (se) doubles as by for any means: बस से (bus se) = by bus. Card se, haath se (by hand) – transport, payment, and tools all take से.

target: सुषमा की किताब मेज़ पर रखी है।
english: Sushma's book is kept on the table.
tip: की (ki) agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: सुषमा की किताब (Sushma ki kitaab) uses feminine की because kitaab is feminine – Sushma's own gender is irrelevant.

target: मेरे ऑफिस में बहुत अच्छे साथी हैं।
english: I have great colleagues in my office.
tip: Hindi has no verb for to have – people just exist in your space: मेरे ऑफिस में बहुत अच्छे साथी हैं (mere office mein bahut achche saathi hain = in my office are very good colleagues).

target: एड़ी में दर्द होने से चलना मुश्किल था।
english: Walking was difficult due to heel pain.
tip: से (se) also marks causes: दर्द होने से (dard hone se = from pain happening) = because of the pain. Verb + hone se is the everyday due to.

target: रास्ते में मेरा फ़ोन बंद हो गया।
english: My phone died on the way.
tip: Phones close in Hindi: फ़ोन बंद हो गया (phone band ho gaya = the phone became closed) = it died or switched off. बंद (band) covers closed and off – shops, lights, phones.

target: बस स्टॉप पर बहुत भीड़ है।
english: There is a big crowd at the bus stop.
tip: पर (par) means on, but it is also Hindi's at: बस स्टॉप पर (bus stop par) = at the bus stop. There is no separate word – station par, ghar par.
